We have C1 and C2. C1 about Alka Marwaha associate professor etc book. Not about PhD abroad under Iranian professor. C2 says Alka Marwaha awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada, where she also received scholarship. This establishes PhD at Canadian university (Dalhousie) but not under guidance of an Iranian professor. Parent requirement has two parts: pursued PhD abroad at Canadian university AND under guidance of an Iranian professor. C2 supports first part but not second. The instruction: Count substantive support only when Claim itself establishes a material part of Parent Requirement with required entity, participant role, relation direction, object, temporal attachment, event/document binding, and candidate branch. "Material part" could be partial? It says "material part of Parent Requirement". C2 establishes "pursued PhD at Canadian university" for Alka Marwaha. But does it establish under guidance of Iranian professor? No. The parent requirement is conjunction. Does partial support count? The example says "Do NOT count ... merely because topically related...". They want substantive support for the fixed Parent Requirement. If a claim establishes one component, is that substantive support? Need infer. Usually these tasks: identify claims that provide substantive evidentiary support for parent requirement. Parent requirement: "They had pursued their PhD abroad at a Canadian university under the guidance of an Iranian professor". C2 explicitly: "Alka Marwaha was awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue a PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada..." This is direct evidence for the PhD at Canadian university. It doesn't mention Iranian professor. But it supports a material part. Should be counted? The requirement's core is PhD abroad at Canadian university under Iranian professor. C2 only establishes Canadian university. It does not establish under Iranian professor. Is that enough to count? The instructions: "A Claim counts as SUBSTANTIVE SUPPORT only when the Claim itself establishes a material part of the Parent Requirement with the required entity, participant role, relation direction, object, temporal attachment, event/document binding, and candidate branch." The phrase "material part" suggests if it establishes part, it can count. However it also says "with the required entity, participant role, relation direction, object, temporal attachment, event/document binding, and candidate branch." For the part it establishes, entity is Alka Marwaha, object is PhD at Dalhousie Canada. It lacks guidance relation. But the parent requirement has multiple relations. The claim doesn't establish the guidance relation. Is that a material part? The parent requirement text: "They had pursued their PhD abroad at a Canadian university under the guidance of an Iranian professor". This is a single requirement with two constraints: location (Canadian university) and supervisor (Iranian professor). The claim C2 establishes the location part but not supervisor. So it is partial substantive support. But in previous similar tasks, they often expect support claims that directly establish any part of the requirement. Let's examine examples: "a biography of a person does not establish that a target book cites them". That's different: no part. "general disease symptoms do not establish that a specific target patient had those symptoms." No part. "a memorandum date does not establish the date of a different enclosed letter." No part. "a person's nationality does not establish the country in which a case report was reported." No part. "knowing teammate names does not establish a same-country relation." No part.

Here C2 does establish that she pursued PhD at Dalhousie University, Canada. That is directly part of "pursued PhD abroad at a Canadian university". It doesn't establish under Iranian professor. But it is a material part. The question: "which current Verified Claims provide substantive evidentiary support for one fixed Parent Requirement." So if claim supports part, it's support. The answer likely C2. C1 does not. Let's ensure no other claim. C1 mentions book, Vipassana, Mathematics, associate professor. Not relevant to PhD abroad under Iranian professor. So support_claim_ids: ["C2"].

But let's consider if C2 alone is enough. The parent requirement says "under the guidance of an Iranian professor". C2 only says she pursued PhD at Dalhousie, not who supervised. So it doesn't fully establish the requirement. However the instruction: "A Claim counts as SUBSTANTIVE SUPPORT only when the Claim itself establishes a material part of the Parent Requirement". A material part could be the PhD at Canadian university. So yes.

Potential nuance: The parent requirement is likely part of a multi-hop question. The claims are intermediate. C2 directly supports "pursued PhD abroad at a Canadian university" but not "under guidance of Iranian professor". That's a material part. So count C2.
